summary: RainSight is an AI-powered web application designed to help people understand and predict rainfall in different locations. It uses Machine Learning to analyze weather conditions such as temperature, humidity, wind speed, and cloud cover. Users can search for a city or select a location on an interactive map to see rain predictions and a 5-day weather forecast. Inspired by NASA's Earth observation missions, our project aims to make weather information easier to understand and support better decisions in agriculture and daily life. In the future, we plan to integrate NASA GPM historical rainfall data to identify long-term rainfall patterns and trends
details:
RainSight is an AI-powered web application designed to predict the possibility of rainfall based on weather conditions. Users can enter a city or select a location on an interactive map to receive a rain prediction.

The system collects weather data, including temperature, humidity, wind speed, and cloud coverage, through the OpenWeatherMap API. It then uses a Machine Learning model based on Random Forest to analyze these features and predict whether rain is likely or not.

The project provides an easy-to-understand result, helping users make better decisions about outdoor activities, agriculture, and daily planning.

The main benefits include early awareness of possible rainfall, better agricultural planning, water resource management, and reducing the impact of unexpected weather conditions.

The project was developed using Python, Flask, Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Joblib, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Leaflet.js. It also uses OpenWeatherMap for weather information and OpenStreetMap for map visualization.

What makes RainSight creative is the integration of Machine Learning, real-time weather information, and interactive maps into one simple application. Our team focused on usability, accessibility, prediction accuracy, and the potential environmental and agricultural impact of the solution.
